AFC Rankings Preseason
stories.summary:
I have done this for a few years now where I rank the AFC with some humor, some honestly, and probably some bad opinions. I typically do this every 3-4 weeks (quarter or so) of the Season so this is my sole one for the preseason. Argue, agree, tell me I have no brain cells lets go:



	 



	Orange Crush



	Denver Broncos- Top to bottom the most complete roster of the AFC and truthfully the team that should’ve made the super bowl in the AFC if not for a broken ankle to Bo Nix. Bo may come back a little on his play after a good year with many 4th quarter heroics, but they properly added at WR with Waddle. They had a high amount of one score wins in 2025 so their record may comeback 1-3 games in W column but still a complete team across the board that no other AFC matches top to bottom..



	 



	MVP QB, New Coach, Sky-high Expectations… Good Luck



	Buffalo Bills & Baltimore Ravens- Same storyline for each team as the sky is the limit as is the expectations. Will Brady with a different vision on offense and defense with Jim get the Bills over the hump so it isn’t all on Josh come playoff time? Can Minter help the Ravens defense return to form and get the Ravens over the hump with Lamar while also not blowing big leads yearly? Not a lot to say because the expectations are at max for both teams and QB, SUPER BOWL OR BUST



	 



	Everyone’s Favorite Darkhorse AFC Champ



	Houston Texans- I am myself a big Texas believer, so much hinges on that offense being decently competent and more importantly the offensive line blocking for Stroud to not die and the RBs to run. Still this probably is the scariest team in the AFC simply because the defense will keep them in every game where the offense just needs to be OK.



	 



	The Skeptics Exist But These Are Good Teams On Paper



	New England Patriots- Year 3 for the Maye-Flower and even with some regression and a tougher schedule he still should help carry the Pats. The big question is more how the remainder of the roster does and when attrition hits how they handle it.



	Jacksonville Jaguars- Their numbers from the Meyers trade on were fantastic on offense, but there is more there then that. The defense was top 10 in epa, the offense has a plethora of WRs, the coaching is quite good, and the play in a favorable division besides HOU. Can they have back to back winning seasons for the first time in two decades.



	 



	Reasons To Buy & Reasons To Be Wary



	Los Angeles Chargers- So they get back their starting offensive line men who were out all year, McDaniel feels like a step above Roman, they have made the playoffs three of the last four years winning 11 games the last two with Harbaugh. Yet why does it feel like we’ve been waiting for a bigger breakthrough that never happens and it is just excuses for the quarterback when the brass numbers show he ain’t doing it. Oh and no one is discussing how good Minter was as DC for this team who just left.



	Cincinnati Bengals- The defense looks improved on paper finally where Burrow is not having to score 40 pts a week which is good. Speaking of Burrow though he has started 35 games out of 51 the last three years. I do believe CIN puts it together enough to get back in the post season, but I get those who see another .500ish year.



	Kansas City Chiefs- The laws of nature bounced back big time as the team which had every break go their way in 2024 had it go the opposite way in 2025. They actually were a 10 win team by advanced metrics, but this is not the 2021 team either. The offense should be a bit better, but the defense feels like a shell of its oldself. Still are you betting against Reid/Mahomes to miss back to back years



	 



	They Will Win 7 to 9 Games And Waste Everyone’s Time



	Indianapolis Colts & Pittsburgh Steelers- Both teams were better off breaking the walls down to the studs for some true renovation. Instead the Steelers are playing Madden 2018 apparently and the Colts are gambling on Daniel Jones… to recover from an ACL and play the high level he showed for 8 games before injury. I look at both of these teams and remember what the drought felt like. One of them will be around the playoff picture come December and the other is going to be at 3-4 wins finally asking the hard questions they should’ve last off season or frankly for years prior.



	 



	The Rebuild Is On



	Tennessee Titans- They are pluckier than people think and if Ward can take a step with the new WRs he has and better coaching they could be a sneaky wild card/in the hunt style team come December. That would be huge progress for them after the last bunch of years. Also Saleh is a very good defensive mind and that Jets defense tanked the moment he left. The pieces on the D could be fun for him.



	 



	Oakland sorry Vegas Raiders- The longer Mendoza sits the better it will help his development short term. If it isn’t until week 7-8 this could be one of those annoying teams come week 15-16 that are making games maddening against higher opponents that you’d expect a blow out. They still need a lot of talent, but this year is all about growing their kid at QB and giving hope to the future.



	 



	On To The 2027 Draft



	NY Jets / Miami Dolphins- Jets will win 3-5 games blowing their draft position while the Dolphins could be historically bad on offense despite some nice pieces on defense. Yikes.



	 



	Whatever the Browns Are



	Cleveland Browns- I hate this team. I have seen three year olds with a better plan for the day then whatever their doing here. They will win 3-4 games, the defense will do some things, and they will against make the wrong moves over and over and over. I feel for their fans but what is left to say anymore. Even when they had a halfway decent starter in Baker they ran him out and blew everything up for Watson. Their fans forever deserve better but I just don’t see it happening anytime soon. The front office makes the 49ers medical staff look competent by comparison.

stories.title: Training camp day 8 (back in OP)
Observations about where we think the Bills are
stories.summary:
I find it interesting that there is so little actual football conversation going on this forum at this time of the year. There was less chatter than usual about training camp, and it was dead here between OTAs and training camp. 



	 



	For me, and I think for many of us posting here, I know pretty much what the roster is going to look like and there's not much more to be said about. I know that this should be a good team, competitive at the highest levels. Sure, I can imagine scenarios where things come apart, but any of that is just speculation. 



	 



	I'm just waiting, hoping for no injuries. Maybe one more interesting free agent signing. All the things that I really want to know about the team - how good will the defense be?, how much difference will Moore make?, will Josh take even one more step toward true greatness?, does Brady have what it takes to be a winning head coach? - are things that I can't begin to learn until the regular season gets under way.



	 



	Until then, I'm just waiting.

DJ Moore is going to be an "Elite WR" this season
stories.summary:
Writing is on the wall.



	 



	Now that we've gone through OTAs, minicamp and the St. John portion of TC, it's pretty clear the chemistry between Allen and Moore is reminiscent of Allen and Diggs when Diggs came in 2020.



	 



	No, I don't see Moore leading the NFL in receptions & receiving yards. Buffalo has better secondary weapons than we did in 2020 and Allen’s growth as a QB who sees the field so well is going to spread the ball around more than in 2020.



	 



	But I also think we're going to pass a good bit more than the last couple years and with Moore we no longer have to fall back on Mesh in those 3rd down gotta have it moments. 



	 



	Moore can still clearly get open. From all the reports it sounds like his worst rep of camp was against Benford who got an INT because Moore slipped on the wet grass in the rain. Sounds like it was a physical rep, but Moore slipped.



	 



	And I think we'll continue to revisit the whole "DJ Moore is washed!!!" narrative, but I spent a bored Friday evening (my life is so exciting) watching highlights of every single year of his career.



	 



	I just don't see a washed or diminished player. Honestly, his skillset excites me more than what we had with Diggs. Moore is a true all over the field threat. Diggs was, too, but Moore's at his best downfield. That wasn't Diggs.



	 



	Plus there's the speed and YAC ability.



	 



	I just think it all fits with Allen and this offense and we're going to hear a lot of backtracking nationally this coming season about DJ Moore the player and the cost to acquire him.

stories.summary: Just curious if anyone here is renewing their Sunday Ticket from last year. Last year because I was a new customer, I only paid around $200 for the package. This year since I would be a returning customer, it's going to cost me $480 which I really have no intention of paying. My question here is to the people that are renewing that don't have Youtube TV, have you reached out to YouTube and tried to haggle with them like with Directv to see if you could get it at a cheaper rate? And if so, is YouTube biting? I currently do not have YouTube TV so unlike when I had Directv and could just simply threaten to cancel to get a discount. I can't do that with Youtube TV. I bought the subscription separately and it looks like if I decided to get YouTube TV with it, I could actually renew Sunday Ticket for $240 but that's on top of paying $54 a month for the YouTube TV subscription. Has anyone been able to get a discount on a renewal with just the Sunday Ticket subscription? And if so, what did you do to make it happen?
